original_question: Does there exist a measurable set Omega subset R with 0 < mes(Omega) < +infinity such that its indicator function 1_Omega tiles R by translations over a set Lambda subset R that does not have periodic structure, either at level one or, more weakly, at some other integer level w? Here, not having periodic structure means that Lambda cannot be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j with a_j > 0.
target_in_paper: Section 6.2 (Non-periodic tilings), second open question: Does there exist a measurable set Ω ⊂ R, 0 < mes(Ω) < +∞, whose indicator function 1_Ω can tile at level one, or, more weakly, at some other integer level w, with a translation set Λ ⊂ R that does not have a periodic structure?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact open problem. It correctly identifies the ambient space R, the measurable set Ω with 0 < mes(Ω) < +∞, the indicator function 1_Ω, the possibility of tiling at level 1 or at some integer level w, and the intended meaning of 'no periodic structure' as failure of representation by finitely many disjoint arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j with a_j > 0. It also stays on the paper’s narrower indicator-function version rather than drifting to the broader neighboring question for general f ∈ L^1(R).
missing_details: The paper assumes the translation set Λ is a discrete set of bounded density; this bounded-density hypothesis is part of the Section 6.2 question and is missing from the draft.

To be fully stand-alone, the tiling relation should be stated explicitly: Σ_{λ∈Λ} 1_Ω(x−λ) = 1 almost everywhere, or more generally = w almost everywhere for some integer w, with the series converging absolutely almost everywhere, as in the paper’s definition of tiling.

The paper’s terminology 'periodic structure' is defined earlier by the exact form Λ = ⨆_{j=1}^N (a_j Z + b_j), a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions with real parameters a_j > 0 and b_j ∈ R; the draft gives this, but not the fact that this is the paper’s named definition from equation (1.4).

The question is posed as a special case of the immediately preceding broader open problem in Section 6.2: whether any nonzero f ∈ L^1(R) whose nonzero set has finite measure must force Λ to have periodic structure. That nearby context helps fix the intended scope.
The paper notes that if such an Ω exists, then Ω must be unbounded, by Theorem 1.5; this is not part of the formal question itself, but it is an important nearby constraint in the paper’s discussion.
refined_question: Does there exist a measurable set Ω ⊂ R with 0 < mes(Ω) < +∞ and a discrete translation set Λ ⊂ R of bounded density, such that either Σ_{λ∈Λ} 1_Ω(x−λ) = 1 for almost every x ∈ R, or, more weakly, Σ_{λ∈Λ} 1_Ω(x−λ) = w for almost every x ∈ R for some integer w, where the series converges absolutely almost everywhere, and such that Λ does not have periodic structure, i.e. Λ cannot be written as a disjoint union Λ = ⨆_{j=1}^N (a_j Z + b_j) with finitely many real numbers a_j > 0 and b_j?
justification: The draft is targeting the second question in Section 6.2, page 20, almost verbatim. That section first asks a broader open problem for general nonzero f ∈ L^1(R) whose nonzero set has finite measure, and then specializes to the indicator-function case for measurable Ω of finite positive measure. The paper’s definition of tiling is given in Section 1, equation (1.1), and its definition of 'periodic structure' is given in Section 1.3, equation (1.4). Theorem 1.5 explains why compactly supported tiling functions force periodic structure, which is why Section 6.2 explicitly focuses on finite-measure support rather than compact support; the paper also notes on page 20 that any such Ω would have to be unbounded. Theorems 1.7 and 1.8 show that non-periodic tilings do exist for more general L^1 functions, so the unresolved issue here is specifically whether such behavior can occur for an indicator function 1_Ω.
